procedure.description: panniculectomy with excision of excess skin and subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen

denial.carcText: Benefit maximum for this time period or occurrence has been reached.
denial.text: Northwind Mutual Health denied the claim for CPT 15847 (panniculectomy with excision of excess skin and subcutaneous tissue of the abdomen) with date of service 2026-05-04. CARC 119: Benefit maximum for this time period or occurrence has been reached. Payer remark: The outpatient surgical benefit maximum for the plan year has been exhausted.

criteria.text: Panniculus hangs at or below the level of the pubis (grade 2 or higher) as documented on examination.

Recurrent or chronic intertrigo, cellulitis, or skin breakdown beneath the panniculus that has failed at least 3 months of conservative treatment such as topical antifungals, hygiene measures, and barrier products.
Weight stable within 10 pounds for at least 6 months.
The panniculus interferes with activities of daily living or ambulation.

chart.text: Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.

Twisted the right ankle stepping off a curb 2 days ago. Swelling over the lateral malleolus, tender over the ATFL, can bear weight. Ottawa negative, no film. Brace, ice, ibuprofen, elevate. Should be fine in a couple weeks.
Vitamin D came back 14. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Referral letter from the primary care office. Thank you for seeing this patient of mine for surgical evaluation. Her history and medication list are attached. Please let me know what you recommend and whether anything is needed from our end for clearance.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 20. Approved 90 days. She mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.

46 year old woman here about the abdominal apron after her weight loss. Nice result on the weight. Discussed panniculectomy versus a full abdominoplasty and what insurance will and will not look at. Her history otherwise: seasonal allergies, mild asthma, albuterol maybe twice a year. Allergies: codeine makes her sick. Never smoked, occasional beer, has three kids at home. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. On exam the pannus hangs well below the pubis, I would call it grade 2, with maceration and an odor in the fold. She has been fighting the rash under the apron for better than a year, treated with nystatin, then clotrimazole, keeps it dry with powder and a cloth liner, and it comes right back. Two rounds of antibiotics from the PCP for cellulitis in the fold. Down 123 pounds after the sleeve in 2023. Weight has been steady at 181 give or take five for the last 11 months. Says she cannot walk more than a block without the skin fold chafing raw, has to lift it to wash underneath, cannot find pants that fit over it.
She called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the fall. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Blood pressure check. 130 over 81 today, 130 over 81 on repeat. She has been taking the lisinopril 20 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 8 weeks.

Follow-up on the abdomen. Went back over the operation, drains, the scar, recovery of four to six weeks. She understands this is skin and fat removal for the skin problems, not a tummy tuck. Vitals today 133 over 73, pulse 85. Rash is back again despite 11 months of the antifungal and barrier routine. Fold is red and weeping today. Weight 184 today, holding.
She called asking where things stand with the insurance. Told her the paperwork went in and we are waiting to hear. Reviewed what to do in the meantime.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, she remains sure about going ahead.

Ear fullness and muffled hearing on the left for a week after a cold. Canal clear, drum dull with fluid behind it, no infection. Serous otitis. Decongestant, swallow and yawn, recheck in three weeks if not better.
A1c came back 6.5. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. She is motivated.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Called her with the cholesterol results. Total 223, LDL 152, HDL 58, triglycerides 169. Discussed diet and walking. She wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Pre-op. Consent signed. Marked the resection with her standing. Nicotine negative. Hold the metformin the morning of.

expected.note: CARC 119 is an administrative denial the chart cannot answer: the remedy is a benefits dispute under the plan document, not a medical necessity appeal.
